done_when: Find which one it is: if Forge can return before the app-server process exits, make it wait for the exit; if it's only the check, make the test tell a leftover process from a reused PID. test_4_turn_log passes on Windows CI three runs in a row

findings.body: A failed identity lookup makes the leak assertion pass: empty stdout becomes `None`, so `_left(recorded_server)` returns false even if the server remains alive. On Windows, a nonterminating `Get-CimInstance` error also reaches `exit 3` because this script omits `$ErrorActionPreference = 'Stop'`. The production query explicitly distinguishes these cases in `src/forge/codex.py:310–324`, and `tests/test_codex_record.py:267–269` exercises this query-failure scenario. Make unexpected query failures fail the test, and return `None` only when the query successfully establishes that the PID is absent.
findings.title: Reject failed process queries instead of treating them as process exit

why: tests/test_codex_worker.py::test_4_turn_log fails on Windows CI about one run in two: right after forge work returns, tasklist still lists one of the four reported Codex app-server PIDs (either Forge returns before the process has fully exited on Windows, or Windows reused the PID)
